argument: Every one of sixteen closed message types is in one already-permitted function or is the existing cross-cutting refusal. Unknown members/types/enums cannot add a semantic act: they are RF2.
Wrong direction, state, sequence and correlation refuse as RF7, with lawful-direction replay RF8. No valid frame acquires another function through a bad direction.

All free text and opaque references are inert data. Resolving an operation reference selects an existing separately validated host broker record; it never evaluates source text or a command string. The declared HE1/HE2 registry permits only staged operational/cache state writes and project reads. References outside authorized scope fail RF6 under the host permission decision.

Thus no schema-valid, state-valid message can ask the control plane to interpret/transform/adjudicate provider semantics. RF5 has no locally generatable trigger in this preview schema. Receiving a frozen refusal whose family is RF5 remains syntactically lawful and terminal; future reviewed vocabulary/function successors must explicitly decide reachability.
supersedes: Accepted CC8/RF5 prose only insofar as it appears to require a reachable schema-valid semantic-content request despite the completed closed preview body/effect registry. Universal ban on control interpretation of provider semantics remains.
noOracle: No Boolean semanticActionRequested or NLP classifier may be used as evidence of a concrete forbidden act.
